Speaker's Card/Request to Speak:
If you would like to address the City Council/Board of Directors on a scheduled agenda item, including a Consent Calendar item, a Regular Council/Board Business item, a Public Hearing item, or Public Comments, please complete the "Request to Speak Form." The card is at the table at the entrance to the City Council Chamber. Please identify on the card your name and the item on which you would like to speak and return to the City Clerk. The "Request to Speak Form" assists the Mayor/Chair in ensuring that all persons wishing to address the City Council/Board of Directors are recognized. It also ensures the accurate identification of meeting participants in the City Council/Board minutes. Your name will be called at the time the matter is heard by the City Council/Board of Directors. City policy is to limit public testimony to up to three minutes per speaker depending on relevant circumstances (unless the time limit is extended by the Mayor/Chair), which includes the presentation of electronic or audio visual information. Speakers may not yield their time to other persons.
Please take notice that
the order of scheduled agenda items below and/or the time they are actually heard, considered and decided may be modified by the Mayor/Chair or the City Council/Board of Directors during the course of the meeting, so please stay alert.

NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
LIVE BROADCASTING AND REBROADCASTING
Regular City Council meetings are broadcast live every 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month at 4 p.m. and are replayed on Tuesdays at 4 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live City Council meeting), Sundays at 11 a.m., Wednesdays at 7 p.m., and Thursdays at 7 p.m. until the next City Council meeting. Regular Orange County Great Park Board meetings are broadcast live every 4th Tuesday of the month at 2 p.m. and are replayed on Wednesdays at 8 p.m., Thursdays at 10 a.m., and Saturdays at 7 p.m. (in weeks in which there is not a live Orange County Great Park meeting) until the next Orange County Great Park Board meeting. All broadcasts can be viewed on Cox Communications Local Access Channel 30 and U-Verse Channel 99. City Council meetings are also available via live webcast and at any time for replaying through the Cityâ€™s ICTV webpage at cityofirvine.org/ictv. For more information, please contact the Clerk of the Board/City Clerkâ€™s office at (949) 724-6205.
STAFF REPORTS
As a general rule, staff reports or other written documentation have been prepared or organized with respect to each item of business listed on the agenda. Copies of these materials are on file with the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board and are available for public inspection and copying once the agenda is publicly posted, (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council/Great Park Board meeting). Staff reports can also be downloaded from the Cityâ€™s website at cityofirvine.org and the Orange County Great Park website at ocgp.org beginning the Friday prior to the scheduled City Council/Orange County Great Park Board meeting on Tuesday.
In addition, meetings can be viewed live at the time posted on the agenda and related staff reports can be opened and viewed simultaneously along with the streaming of the meeting. To view the meeting, go to cityofirvine.org/ictv.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUPPLEMENTAL MATERIAL RECEIVED AFTER THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA
Any supplemental writings or documents distributed to a majority of the City Council/Orange County Great Park Board regarding any item on this agenda after the posting of the agenda will be available for public review in the City Clerk/Clerk of the Boardâ€™s Office, One Civic Center Plaza, Irvine, California, during normal business hours. In addition, such writings or documents will be made available for public review at the respective public meeting.
If you have any questions regarding any item of business on the agenda for this meeting, or any of the staff reports or other documentation relating to any agenda item, please contact City Clerk/Clerk of the Board staff at (949)724-6205.
SUBMITTAL OF INFORMATION BY MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC FOR DISSEMINATION OR PRESENTATION AT PUBLIC MEETINGS
Media Types and Guidelines
1. Written Materials/Handouts:
Any member of the public who desires to submit documentation in hard copy form may do so prior to the meeting or at the time he/she addresses the City Council/Orange County Great Park Board. Please provide 15 copies of the information to be submitted and file with the City Clerk/Clerk of the Board at the time of arrival to the meeting. This information will be disseminated to the City Council/Orange County Great Park Board at the time testimony is given.
2. Large Displays/Maps/Renderings:
Any member of the public who desires to display freestanding large displays or renderings in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to notify the City Clerk/Clerk of the Boardâ€™s Office at (949)724-6205 no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting so that an easel can be made available, if necessary.
3. Electronic Documents/Audio-Visuals:
Any member of the public who desires to display information electronically in conjunction with their public testimony is asked to submit the information to the Public Information Office (PIO) no later than 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting. To facilitate your request contact the PIO Office at (949)724-6253 or the City Clerkâ€™s Office at (949)724-6205.
Information must be provided on CD, DVD, or VHS; or, emailed by 12:00 noon on the day of the scheduled meeting to pio@ci.irvine.ca.us. Members of the public will be asked to provide their name, identify the meeting and the agenda item to be addressed, and a day time phone number.
The PIO office will notify the person submitting the information as soon as possible prior to the meeting if the information cannot be accessed or if the version provided is incompatible with the Cityâ€™s system. Every effort will be made by City staff to facilitate the presentation.
CITY SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS
It is the intention of the City of Irvine to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA) in all respects. If, as an attendee or a participant at this meeting, you will need special assistance beyond what is normally provided, the City of Irvine will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner. Please contact the City Clerk/Clerk of the Boardâ€™s Office at (949)724-6205.
Assisted listening devices are available at the meeting for individuals with hearing impairments. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35. 104 ADA Title II)
CHALLENGING CITY DECISIONS
The time limit within which to commence any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City is governed by Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure, unless a shorter limitations period is specified by any other provision. Under Section 1094.6, any lawsuit or legal challenge to any quasi-adjudicative decision made by the City must be filed no later than the 90th day following the date on which such decision becomes final. Any lawsuit or legal challenge that is not filed within this 90-day period will be barred.
If a person wishes to challenge the nature of the above actions in court, they may be limited to raising only those issues they or someone else raised at the meeting described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City of Irvine, at or prior to the meeting. In addition, judicial challenge may be limited or barred where the interested party has not sought and exhausted all available administrative remedies.
COMMUNICATION AND ELECTRONIC DEVICES
To minimize distractions, please be sure all personal communication and electronic devices are turned off or on silent mode.
MEETING SCHEDULE
Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesdays of each month at 4:00 p.m. Study Sessions and/or Closed Sessions are periodically held prior to the start of the regular meeting. CALL TO ORDER

The regular meeting of the Irvine City Council was called to order at 4:29 p.m. on June
12, 2018 in the City Council Chamber, Irvine Civic Center, One Civic Center Plaza,
Irvine, California; Mayor Wagner presiding.

  Present:  5  Councilmember:  Melissa Fox
  Councilmember:  Jeffrey Lalloway
  Councilmember:  Christina Shea
  Mayor Pro Tempore:  Lynn Schott
  Mayor:  Donald P. Wagner
 Joint City Council / Great Park Board Minutes  June 12, 2018

  1.  CLOSED SESSION

  Orange County Registrar of Voters, et al., Orange County Superior

  RECESS

  Mayor Wagner convened the regular City Council meeting to Closed Session at
  4:31 p.m.

  RECONVENE TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  Mayor Wagner reconvened the regular City Council meeting at 6:20 p.m. City Attorney
  Melching, on behalf of the City Council, announced that no reportable action was taken
  in Closed Session.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Lalloway led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  2
 Joint City Council / Great Park Board Minutes  June 12, 2018

  INVOCATION

  Senior Pastor Jason Aguilar from the Cloud Church in Irvine provided the invocation.

  2.  PRESENTATIONS

  2.1  2/11 Marine Adoption Committee Annual Update

  Mayor Wagner introduced members of the 2nd Battalion, 11th Marine
  Regiment, 1st Marine Division Committee, who provided an update on
  activities and accomplishments over the past year.

  Following Item 2.1, Mayor Wagner reordered the agenda to consider Public Comments
  prior to Item 2.2. See Public Comments (page 14).

  2.2  Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District Update

  Councilmember Schott, as the City’s representative to the Orange County
  Mosquito and Vector Control District (OCMVCD), introduced OCMVCD
  District Manager Rick Howard and Communications Director Lora Young,
  who provided an update on efforts to control mosquitos and other vectors
  in the City of Irvine and the County of Orange.

  City Council discussion included: inquiring about when a large problem
  with mosquitos and other vectors is determined and how to solve the
  issue; inquired about heartworms and the associated dangers to the
  animal population; expressed concern about how aerial spraying with crop
  dusters kills other species during the process, and questioned how the
  use of aerial spraying is assessed and utilized; reiterated that OCMVCD
  has not initiated the use of aerial spraying since its inception; noted that
  mosquito-eating fish for residential ponds and fountains were available at
  no charge at OCMVCD; and recognized OCMVCD for its Excellence
  Award by the California Department of Pesticide Regulation for its vector
  management plan.

  CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  There was no report.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS/COMMITTEE REPORTS/COUNCIL REPORTS

  Councilmember Lalloway expressed his appreciation to those who provided public
  comment and spoke on the Veterans Cemetery; and noted that he had submitted a
  memo earlier in the day requesting that the item be agendized for the June 26, 2018
  City Council meeting for consideration of relocating the Veterans Cemetery back to the
  Amended and Restated Development Agreement (ARDA) site.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  3
 Joint City Council / Great Park Board Minutes  June 12, 2018

  Councilmember Fox expressed appreciation to Community Services and Public Safety
  staff who contributed to the success of the Irish Fair held this past weekend at the
  Orange County Great Park; and made the following announcement:

    The City has recently been elevated to the Gold Tier Level in the Orange
  County Cities Energy Leadership Partnership in recognition of energy
  savings from the City’s conversion of 680 illuminated street name signs
  and 700 safety light fixtures to LED lamps, which is expected to save
  380,000 kilowatt hours of energy annually and $39,000 in utility costs
  annually. Having received more than $104,000 in rebates for the
  conversion, the City’s capital investment is expected to be paid back in
  less than four years through combined labor and utility cost savings.
  Achieving Gold Tier level enables the City to receive additional rebate
  dollars on future eligible energy efficiency projects.

  Mayor Wagner provided a brief report on his recent trip to Boston for the annual U.S.
  Conference of Mayors, which included topics such as housing and homelessness, youth
  engagement, and autonomous vehicles; and made the following announcements:

    More than 6,000 visitors attended the Super Pet Adoption event, and more
  than 320 animals were adopted. The event featured 34 area rescues, 29
  vendors, and was sponsored by eight area businesses. Animal Care Center
  volunteers and those from other organizations also gave more than 470
  hours of their time to make the event a success. Sponsorships and
  donations received at the event will benefit the Center’s Third Chance for
  Pets and Enhanced Care programs. For information or to see all of the
  Center’s adoptable animals, visit irvineanimals.org.

    The annual Greater Irvine Chamber of Commerce’s annual luncheon with
  the Mayor will be held on Wednesday, June 20 at 11:30 a.m. at Hotel Irvine.
  The luncheon will celebrate the City’s thriving business community,
  recognizing local businesses that have demonstrated the principles of
  community service, volunteerism, and the best traditions of good corporate
  citizenship. Some of the City’s achievements to date, which include updates
  on the development of the Orange County Great Park and transportation
  improvements, will be shared. For information and tickets to the luncheon,
  visit greaterirvinechamber.org.

    The City of Irvine’s largest group swim lesson will take place on Friday,
  June 22 at William Woollett Jr. Aquatics Center. The Super Swim Lesson is
  an effort to educate parents and children about water safety and spread the
  message that “Swimming Lessons Save Lives.” Children three years of age
  and older of all swimming abilities can participate in the free lesson. Check-
  in begins at 5:30 p.m. with the lesson starting at 6 p.m. Registration is
  required. For information, call 949-724-6717.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  4
 Joint City Council / Great Park Board Minutes  June 12, 2018

    The popular “Movies on the Lawn” series is underway at the Orange County
  Great Park begins on Friday, June 22 with Stagecoach, starring John
  Wayne. Other classic films include Brigadoon and Clambake on Fridays,
  and blockbuster hits such as Ferdinand, The LEGO Ninjago Movie, Peter
  Rabbit, and The Greatest Showman on Saturdays as part of the free
  summer pastime. Food trucks will be available at 6:30 p.m., and movies
  begin at dusk. For information and a schedule of films, visit ocgp.org.

  ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS

  There were no additions or deletions to the agenda.

  Prepared by the City Clerk’s Office  5

  ACTION:
  1)  Approved Mayor Pro Tempore Shea's requests for Community
  Partnership Fund Grant nomination in the amount of $1,350 to Irvine
  2/11 Marine Adoption Committee in support of program costs.
  (Contract No. 10233)
  2)  Approved Councilmember Fox's requests for Community Partnership

  $1,500, and Irvine 2/11 Marine Adoption Committee in the amount of
  $1,000, both in support of program costs. (Contract Nos. 10234 and
  10233)
  3)  Authorized the City Manager to prepare and sign the funding
  agreements listed in Actions 1 and 2.

  RECESS

  Mayor Wagner recessed the regular City Council meeting at 8:25 p.m.

  CONVENE TO THE SPECIAL JOINT MEETING

  Mayor/Chairman Wagner convened to the Special Joint Meeting with the Orange
  County Great Park Board at 8:26 p.m. All Councilmembers and Great Park Board
  Directors were present.

  4.  CITY COUNCIL / BOARD BUSINESS

  4.1  CITY OF IRVINE FISCAL YEAR 2018-19 BUDGET

  Grace Leung, Acting City Manager; Pete Carmichael, Director of
  Community Development and Interim Director of the Orange County Great
  Park; and Manuel Gomez, Director of Public Works, presented the staff
  report and responded to questions. Kristin Griffith, Director of
  Administrative Services, was also available for questions.

  City Council/Board discussion included: inquiring about the balance in the

  This item was agendized at the request of Councilmembers Fox and
  Schott, who asked for City Council consideration of designating the Irvine
  Set-Aside funds for the Heritage Library project, providing that any
  additional remaining funds be allocated to other library projects in the City.

  most heavily used library in Orange County, as well as the need to
  renovate and modernize the facility; and suggested deferring the item to
  the next City Council meeting to provide more clarity on the Memorandum
  of Understanding and available funding.
